thread.title: Ayeni, Leath, and Dumas receive all-conference honors for Delaware track and field
thread.title_full: Ayeni, Leath, and Dumas receive all-conference honors for Delaware track and field

author: First State Times
title: Ayeni, Leath, and Dumas receive all-conference honors for Delaware track and field
text:
Throws athlete Olamide Ayeni, sprints athlete Lauren Leath, and middle-distance runner Kadence Dumas from the University of Delaware track and field program received Conference USA all-conference honors for their performances at the outdoor championships held from May 14-16, according to a May 20 announcement by the league.
The recognition highlights strong performances by these athletes during the championship. All-conference honors are awarded to top performers in each event based on their results at the conference meet.
Leath earned first team all-conference honors after winning the 400-meter hurdles with a time of 59.63 seconds. She is the first Blue Hens athlete to win this event at a conference championship. Her time is also a new personal best and ranks second in program history. Leath previously earned a silver medal as part of the distance medley relay team at the Coastal Athletic Association indoor championships.
Ayeni was named to the first team after winning the discus throw with a mark of 55.10 meters, which is her personal best and ranks second all-time in school history. The mark also ties for thirty-ninth best in Division I competition this season. Last year, Ayeni won first place in discus at the CAA outdoor championships and earlier this winter received third team all-conference honors for shot put.
Dumas secured third team all-conference recognition following her third-place finish in the 800-meter run with a personal best time of 2:06.29—also ranking second in program history. This marks Dumas’s third bronze medal in this event; she placed third at both the 2024 and 2025 CAA outdoor championships.
The full list of honorees can be viewed on Conference USA’s official site. The university encourages fans to follow Delaware track and field on X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and Facebook for updates.
